sarah-support: Heads up - we just started seeing a sharp spike of 502/504s from hosted-api in eu1 at ~07:12 UTC. Multiple customers complaining streaming fails and timeouts. sample trace id: tx-0a1b2c3d

leo-eng-sre: Confirmed on our side. Grafana shows error rate jump to ~1.2k/min for ~3m. Upstream envoy stats show a lot of resets and upstream_cx_overflow spikes. Deploy-bot shows a model swap at 07:10 UTC (canary -> v2.3).

sarah-support: Customer repro (short):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
     -d '{"input":"<large payload with metadata>"}' 
     https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```
Response: connection reset / 502 on client side after 30s, sometimes 504.

mike-runtime: Quick capture: envoy (frontdoor) logs show upstream reset with reason "connection failure" and downstream saw "early_response_closed". midproxy h2 pool counters: `upstream_cx_overflow: 712`, `upstream_rq_pending_overflow: 430`. Also seeing a burst of auth-cache misses.

anna-devex: I pulled auth-cache logs around 07:10-07:15 - there was a token rotation event that produced a mass cache-miss storm (many tenants revalidated at once). Auth service backend latency concurrently climbed to ~800ms.

leo-eng-sre: Putting pieces together: token rotation -> auth-cache miss -> auth-backend slow -> frontdoor envoys stalled waiting on auth results for streaming handshakes -> connection pools back up -> upstream_cx_overflow -> 502s/504s. Also noticed some requests carrying unusually large billing/metadata headers (~12KB) which likely made some envoys reject or reset early (header size > configured limit).

sarah-support: That matches customer reports — higher failure rate for long-lived streams and for embedding requests that include tenant metadata. Can we reproduce?

mike-runtime: Running a small repro now: spin up repeated streaming requests with auth token expiry simulated + large metadata headers. Repro consistently triggers early resets after ~25-35s and envoys report `header_too_large` on a subset.

leo-eng-sre: Mitigation steps applied:
- rolled back the canary model swap to reduce additional downstream pressure
- applied temporary splay to auth-rotation so not all tenants refresh at once
- increased midproxy eu1 conn pool soft limit from 200 -> 350 (hotfix)
- bumped frontdoor envoy `buffered_stream_max` and nginx proxy_buffer_size to allow larger headers (temporary)

anna-devex: Also enabled a temporary rate cap on embed chunking for guest tier (throttles oversized requests client-side) and added an auth retry backoff to auth client.

leo-eng-sre: Current status: error rate trending down but still elevated for some tenants. We'll keep the temporary env changes for next 60m while we collect traces and logs. Need a full rollback plan if errors come back.

sarah-support: Customers notified via status page and CS. Quick note: attach trace ids for affected customers: tx-0a1b2c3d, tx-4f5e6d7c, tx-9a0b1c2d.

mike-runtime: Action items:
- collect pcap/traces for 07:05-07:20 window (leo)
- export envoy admin metrics dump (all frontdoor instances in eu1) (mike)
- audit auth-cache eviction/ttl logic and add guardrails (anna)
- create postmortem draft with timeline and customers impacted (sarah)

leo-eng-sre: Quick commands I'm running:
```
# envoy stats snapshot on frontdoor pod
kubectl -n infra logs frontdoor-abc --tail=200 | grep upstream_cx_overflow
# admin dump
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9901/stats?format=json > /tmp/envoy_stats_eu1.json
```

sarah-support: Thanks team. Please @channel when we have the initial postmortem and any customer followups. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Rollback completed for canary v2.3 -> v2.2 at 07:19:12 UTC.

leo-eng-sre: Noted one follow-up: add header-size metrics to frontdoor dashboards and alert if > 8KB. Also add circuit breaker on auth fetch burst to avoid thundering herd.

anna-devex: I'll file a small SDK change to truncate or reject >8KB tenant metadata early with a clear client error to avoid repeat.

sarah-support: Closing thread for now, keeping it pinned until postmortem published.
